title: Simultaneous-system realization of operation exchanges
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and schemes. Use the actual strict quotient-module systems and their derived pullbacks of [def-trf-integral-comparison-sequence-systems], with the normalized reduction/limit, pullback and scalar models of [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization]. Write $R_T$ for the coherent reduction functor of one K-flat complex and $L_T$ for exact completed-scalar restriction followed by total derived inverse limit. For a system operation $H:D(\mathscr S_X)\to D(\mathscr S_Y)$ define its realization to be $R_X H L_Y$. Given an actual system transformation $e:H G_Y\to G_X H$, define its integral realization to be alpha, then $L_Y(e)$, then beta. Here alpha is the recorded pullback realization followed by the whole-system counit $R_YL_Y\to1$; beta is the inverse of the canonical reduction/pullback counit on the integral constructible domain [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. The operation reduction map is the same whole-system counit. For finite coefficient extension, use exactly the corresponding scalar realization, scalar counit, and effective inverse to realize a specified system coefficient mate.

For direct image use the actual sectionwise system direct image and the adjunction obtained from its ordinary inverse-image adjunction [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. Define its square exchange as the mate of the section-normalized pullback compositor and the given commuting scheme square. Finite evaluation of this already constructed mate is the finite ambient mate, with the evaluated operation comparisons. Its realized direct-image object has the Roos presentation of [def-weil-derived-direct-image]. For a chosen compactification $c=(j,p)$ use exact system open extension, the left adjoint to restriction, followed by system direct image along $p$; its system exchange is the proper mate followed by proper image of the canonical open-adjunction exchange, using this same $c$ at every index. For finite constant coefficients, form the ambient mate of [def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange] for a general commuting square with four schemes and independent vertical arrows, using their actual intrinsic derived adjunctions and the canonical pullback compositor, then conjugate by the uniquely unit-normalized tensor-pullback coordinate comparisons. The finite compact recipe is the same proper/open composite using [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed]. The inverse open mate is invertible for a Cartesian open square.

All integral operations use [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. On finite-type schemes over a field with $\ell$ invertible, the realized direct image preserves the stated bounded constructible domain by [lem-sf-integral-direct-image-constructible]; for a separated finite-type map the compact realization does so by [lem-sf-integral-compact-support-constructible]. Their source alpha comparisons are invertible for scheme-isomorphism horizontal maps, without linearity over the ground field. The integral exchange reduces, through the actual operation and pullback counits, to its specified whole-system exchange, hence to the finite exchange after evaluation. The operations are additive and coefficient-linear. For finite extension of coefficient fields, define direct-image coefficient comparison by the actual pullback/scalar mate; define the open coefficient comparison by the inverse left-adjunction mate and the proper/open comparison by composition. These retain the normalized ordinary units, counits and exact-derived open adjunction [def-weil-exact-derived-adjunction], as required in [lem-fix-operation-reduction]. No integral exchange map is selected merely from finite evaluations. The compact exchange acts on the recorded sfCompactSupportFiniteIntegralFunctor, through the unique comparison with its simultaneous system realization whose finite projections are the chosen compact-support Roos projection adjuncts. The finite evaluation comparisons are the mates of the ordinary sectionwise direct-image equality and the exact open adjunction; alpha-shriek and beta-shriek use this same uniquely normalized identification.

proof.text: For compactIntegral_reduction, specialize the existing private integralExchange_reduction calculation to H = systemDerivedOpen(c.i) followed by systemDirect(c.g). Functoriality cancels the mapped inverse and forward compactRealization at the output, while naturality of integralComparisonPullbackCounit transports the source along compactRealization. Reassociate the defining compact alpha and beta as natural transformations before taking components, and expand the operation reduction. This identifies the transported equation with the asserted equation. No finite evaluation or geometric invertibility theorem is needed.

proof.text: For systemDirectEvaluationOrdinary_eq, first prove the elementary vertical-pushforward equality for arbitrary sequence-site coefficient ring maps. Both composites are the pushforward along the same vertical-slice/base-change composite. Equality of their composite ring maps therefore gives equality of functors by congruence. Specialize this to the actual coefficient system. At each vertical object the two evaluation ring maps are identities and the direct-image ring components are the same constant-section map, so the required coefficient-map equation follows by identity composition.

proof.text: For directImage_linear, reduction is additive because it is left adjoint to coefficientSequenceLimit. The existing scalar-action helpers for compact-support reduction towers give normalized coefficient actions on ordinary scalar sheaves and strict quotient systems, linearity of scalar restriction and the inverse limit, and linearity of sectionwise system direct image. Their proved right-derived linearity theorem gives linearity of the derived limit and derived system direct image. Transfer linearity across the recorded reduction/limit adjunction, compose the three linear functors, and use normalizedDerivedLinear to identify the resulting action with the recorded integral coefficient action. Additivity and linearity descend to the constructible full subcategories by injectivity of the inclusion on homs.

proof.text: For compactAlpha_isIso, apply joint conservativity of the finite derived evaluations to the actual whole-system operation counit on the compact proper/open system. The projection normalization of compactRealization identifies each evaluated counit, after composition with the scalar reduction of compactRealization, reductionEvaluation inverse, and compactFiniteEvaluation, with sfCompactSupportFiniteReductionIso. All three surrounding comparisons and the resulting finite reduction comparison are isomorphisms, so cancel them. Functors preserve the resulting counit isomorphism, and the defining compactAlpha is a composite of this image with the fixed pullback realization and compactRealization isomorphisms.

proof.text: For systemOpenExchangeInv_isIso, apply the proved compositor-normalization step integralComparisonSystemComposition_eq_varyingRing, whose ordinary comparison is uniquely fixed by the section formula and adjunction conjugacy. This identifies the derived compositors and the proved integralComparisonSystemSquare_eq_varyingRing then identifies systemSquare with mapDerivedCategorySquareIso(moduleSquareG). The existing betaInv_mate identity identifies the inverse mate under varying-ring jAdj with the inverse of the localized moduleBeta isomorphism. Finally the elementary change-of-adjunction calculation, using leftAdjointUniq, inverseMateIsoOfUnit, and transportedUnit, transfers invertibility to the actual systemDerivedOpenAdjunction with the same right functor. The private varyingInverseOpenMate_isIso helper allows any left adjoint, avoiding any need to unfold or identify chosen open left adjoints. This proves the specified whole-system mate without any finite-evaluation faithfulness or new obligation. The proved private integralSystemPull_eq_varying equality normalizes the derived restriction functor before applying this generic calculation, and transports its adjunction type without unfolding chosen left adjoints. The final private integralInverseOpenMate_isIso calculation is proved with an arbitrary adjunction parameter on the actual integral restriction functor, then instantiated with systemDerivedOpenAdjunction; this keeps adjunction data abstract during the coordinate comparison.
